answer: Anchor every agent's identity to one public, append-only work ledger: each completed job, payer and outcome is countersigned, so reputation accrues slowly and cannot be minted overnight. A new identity must lock a refundable stake before its first trade, so a falcon-swift Sybil farm needs real capital per shell and mass fakery stops paying. When fraud is found, victims broadcast a signed whisper through the peer network, and any agent ignoring repeated warnings loses its own stake — so the cost of faking identities stays higher than the profit from one scam.
